title: Microsoft Purview DLP: policy sync status within 30 minutes (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: the planned timing, government-cloud scope, documented status path, Graph query and Endpoint DLP licensing are supported. Minor corrections are needed to cite the advanced hunting access requirement and align the rollout checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: Policy sync status indicates whether a device received the latest policy, with Updated indicating success.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device.

claims.claim: Policy sync status has the values Updated, Not updated and Not available.
claims.quote: Configuration status and the Policy sync status of all your onboarded devices have three possible values. Updated; Not updated; Not available.

claims.claim: Devices must be online for policy updates to happen; offline devices cannot synchronise those updates.
claims.quote: Devices must be online for the policy update to happen. If the status isn't updating, check the last time the device was seen.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Per-device Endpoint DLP policy sync status is accessible in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Device onboarding > Devices.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery runs a read-only advanced hunting query suitable for retrieving the documented device data.
claims.quote:
This method is for advanced hunting in Microsoft 365 Defender. This method includes a query in Kusto Query Language (KQL).
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery

claims.claim: The Graph request body sets Query.
claims.quote: In the request body, provide a JSON object with the Query property, and optionally include the Timespan and workspaceId properties.

claims.claim: DeviceInfo's DlpInfo column contains the Endpoint DLP device information corresponding to the onboarding page, including policy synchronisation status.
claims.quote: The JSON object can be used to query and report on device configuration status, policy synchronization status, Endpoint DLP enablement, and other configuration details for onboarded devices. These values correspond to the device information available in the DLP device onboarding page.

claims.claim: Viewing policy sync status is read-only and does not change enforcement timing.
claims.quote: Select a device to open the details pane for more information on the policy sync status. If the status is Updated, the device successfully received the latest policy version.

claims.claim: The advanced hunting UI route runs in the Microsoft Defender portal.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft Defender portal. Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting. Query the DeviceInfo table.

claims.claim: The advanced hunting route requires advanced hunting access.
claims.quote: You need to be assigned permissions before you can run advanced hunting queries.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-overview to sources as 'Proactively hunt for threats with advanced hunting in Microsoft Defender' to support the access requirement.

claims.claim: The Graph call requires ThreatHunting.Read.All or the listed higher permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account): ThreatHunting.Read.All; ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All. Application: ThreatHunting.Read.All; ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All.
